enrollExisting.description: Whether to enroll contacts who already meet the trigger conditions. When omitted or false, only future trigger events are processed. When `enrollExisting=true`: - **Event-based triggers** (e.g. "placed order", "started checkout"): contacts whose trigger event occurred within the first delay block's time window are enrolled. They receive messages based on their original event time, not when the workflow was enabled (e.g. 30-day delay, event 20 days ago → message in 10 days). The workflow **must** start with a delay block — otherwise the request is rejected with 409 `enroll-existing-not-applicable`. - **"Entered segment" trigger**: all contacts currently in the trigger's segments are enrolled immediately. Takes effect only on the first enable; re-enabling with `enrollExisting=true` is rejected with 409 `enroll-existing-not-applicable`. Copy the workflow if a fresh enrollment is needed. - **Birthday, "Product back in stock", and custom virtual events**: not supported; `enrollExisting=true` is rejected with 409 `enroll-existing-not-applicable`.

InactivitySettings.description: Trigger inactivity time defines how long a contact must remain inactive before the automation triggers. The contact must first match the trigger filters. If the trigger event fires again before the timer expires, the timer resets — ensuring the workflow starts only after the contact has finished their activity. For example, with an "added product to cart" trigger and inactivity set to 1 hour, each cart update resets the timer. The automation triggers only after the cart has not been updated for 1 hour, ensuring the email reflects the shopper's complete cart.

duration.description: Inactivity period — the timer resets on each re-trigger

InactivitySettingsRequest.description: Inactivity settings — fires the workflow only after the contact has gone quiet (no new triggering events) for the given duration. Each new triggering event resets the timer. Use this for abandoned-flow patterns where you want to wait for the contact to *not* complete the next step. Common pairings: abandoned cart (30m after "added to cart"), abandoned checkout (1h after "started checkout"), browse abandonment (30m after "viewed product"), or win-back / re-engagement (e.g. 7d after a key event). Example: `{"duration": {"amount": 30, "units": "m"}}`

duration.description: Inactivity period. Required when inactivitySettings is provided.

SendingThresholds.description: Sending thresholds control which contacts receive messages at each send block (email, SMS, push) based on their subscription status. These settings do not affect which contacts enter the automation — only who receives messages when they reach a send block. Contacts who don't meet the threshold are either skipped or stopped depending on the message block configuration. Threshold levels (from most restrictive to least): - "subscribed": send only to contacts who opted in to receive marketing content. Use for newsletters, promotions, and product updates. - "nonSubscribed": send to subscribed and non-subscribed contacts, excluding those who explicitly unsubscribed. Use for behavior-triggered messages like abandoned cart reminders and post-purchase follow-ups. - "all": send to all contacts regardless of subscription status. Use for transactional content like order confirmations and shipping updates. Push notifications are always restricted to subscribed contacts. When omitted, all channels default to "subscribed". Note: due to US regulations, SMS to US contacts is restricted to subscribed contacts only, regardless of this setting.

To deliver SMS blocks only to SMS subscribers, set `sms` to `"subscribed"` (the default) — `nonSubscribed` and `all` will route SMS to non-subscribed contacts as well, which is rarely desired. Note: due to US regulations (CTIA), SMS to US contacts is always restricted to subscribed contacts only — US non-subscribers will not be reached on the SMS channel regardless of the `sms` value.

SplitFilterRequest.description: Split filter — the `type` discriminator determines which fields and operators are valid. | type | field | operator | value | urlMatch | |---|---|---|---|---| | `event` | event property path (e.g. `total_price`, `cart.items.price`) | `eq`, `neq`, `gt`, `gte`, `lt`, `lte`, `contains`, `notContains`, `startsWith`, `endsWith`, `exists`, `notExists`, `in`, `notIn` | property value | not allowed | | `contact` | contact attribute (`tag`, `country`, `dateAdded`, …) | depends on field — same set as audience contact filters | attribute value | not allowed | | `message` | always `"blockID"` | `openedEmail`, `clickedEmail`, `clickedSms`, `openedPush`, `clickedPush` | ID of a message block above this split | optional for clicked operators (omit to match any click), forbidden for opened operators | For `event` filters, use a property path returned by the [event metadata endpoint](https://api-docs.omnisend.com/v2026-preview/reference/post_event_metadata_query). Choose a numeric property when using numeric operators (`gt`, `gte`, `lt`, `lte`). **Important:** For `event` filters the `value` field's JSON type must match the property's data type. For numeric properties send a JSON number (`"value": 50`); sending a string (`"value": "50"`) returns `400` with a type-mismatch error.

field.description: Property or attribute to filter on. For event filters: event property path. For contact filters: contact attribute name. For message filters: must be "blockID".

operator.description: Comparison or engagement operator. Allowed values depend on the filter type and field.

urlMatch.description: URL match condition. Applies only to clicked message filters (clickedEmail, clickedSms, clickedPush). Must be omitted for event, contact, and opened message filters.

value.description: Filter value. For event filters: must match the property's data type (number for numeric properties, string for string properties); omit only for operators "exists" and "notExists". For contact filters: always a string. For message filters: must be the ID of a message block (email/SMS/push) that appears above this split.

UpdateBlockRequest.description: Automation workflow block for PUT — can create a new block (via temporaryID) or update an existing one (via id). Exactly one of the type-specific fields must be populated based on the type discriminator. **Constraint:** A `delay` block cannot end the workflow. During full block-tree replacement, it may be the final block inside a conditional-split branch when sibling blocks follow the split; those sibling blocks are the shared downstream sequence for both branches. The same applies inside an `abTesting` branch when sibling blocks follow the A/B test block. Otherwise, a delay at the end of a block sequence returns `400`. Conditional-split branches may contain different numbers of blocks. Blocks placed after the split are shared by both branches, allowing them to reconverge into one downstream path.

isTZOptimizationEnabled.description: Whether timezone optimization is enabled. Only available with immediate or scheduled strategy, and only in email campaigns

optimizeFor.description: Optimization objective for personalized sends. Required when strategy is "personalized", must not be set otherwise

respectQuietHours.description: Whether personalized sends avoid contact-local hours from 22:00 through 06:59. If omitted, retains the existing personalized value; defaults to true only when no value exists. Must not be set for other strategies

scheduledAt.description: Campaign scheduled send time in RFC 3339 format. Required when strategy is "scheduled" or "personalized", must not be set for "immediate". For "scheduled" it must be in the future and within one year from now. For "personalized" only the calendar date in the brand timezone is used, not the time-of-day: the value is normalized to the start of that day in the brand timezone. A date resolving to today starts the STO window at the next whole hour when the campaign is sent; a future date (within one year) starts it at brand-local midnight. Per-contact send times are then chosen within the following 24 hours. Responses store the start as brand-local midnight, which can appear as the previous UTC calendar date
